channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Rules for Providing Mobility Aids and Hygiene Products to People with Disabilities
item.description: Kazakhstan has revised its regulations for supplying technical and hygiene products to individuals with disabilities. Recipients will now receive necessary items from the date of application, within an annual quota calculated for 365 days. This includes diapers and mobility aids, with updated procedures for processing applications and proportional distribution for shorter-term needs.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Public Institutions Strengthen Inter-ethnic Harmony, Says Human Rights Commissioner
item.description: Kazakhstan's public institutions actively contribute to strengthening inter-ethnic and interfaith harmony, according to Arthur Lastaev, the Human Rights Commissioner. He highlighted that over 957 ethno-cultural associations and 3,000 public structures operate in the country, fostering civic unity. Constitutional and national laws protect citizens from discrimination based on origin, race, ethnicity, language, or religion.

item.title: CSTO Secretariat Representative Addresses Counter-Terrorism Forum in Minsk
item.description: Umar Umarov, Head of the Department for Countering Challenges and Threats at the CSTO Secretariat, spoke at the Fourth Counter-Terrorism Forum in Minsk. He highlighted the spread of extremist ideology as a significant threat to regional and international security. Umarov emphasized that the CSTO employs a comprehensive mechanism, including operational, preventive, legal, and informational measures, to combat extremism.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Approve Water Distribution Quotas for Amudarya and Syrdarya Rivers for 2026-2027
item.description: Central Asian countries have approved the water distribution quotas for the Amudarya and Syrdarya rivers for the years 2026-2027. Experts discussed water distribution and accounting during a meeting. This agreement aims to manage shared water resources effectively for the upcoming period.

item.title: Son of Kyrgyzstan's Former President Sentenced to Four Years in Prison
item.description: The son of Kyrgyzstan's former president has been sentenced to four years in prison. The specific charges and details of the case were not immediately available. This sentencing follows a legal process involving the former head of state's family member.

item.title: Uzbek President Proposes New Initiatives for Central Asia-Azerbaijan Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev outlined new initiatives for cooperation between Central Asia and Azerbaijan during the eighth consultative meeting of heads of state. Key areas discussed included expanding joint production, developing transport infrastructure, and strengthening collaboration in energy and digital technologies.

item.title: Central Asians Recruited for Work in Russia End Up Fighting in Ukraine Conflict
item.description: Central Asian nationals, including Kazakh citizens, who traveled to Russia for employment opportunities have reportedly been recruited into the Russian military and sent to the combat zone in Ukraine. Families are seeking government assistance to bring their relatives home, with circumstances of their enlistment unclear.

item.title: Afghan Products Gain Interest from Saudi Buyers at Jeddah Food Expo
item.description: Five Afghan businesses showcased agricultural and food products at the Saudi Food Show 2026 in Jeddah, attracting significant interest from Saudi buyers. Products included dried fruits, nuts, and spices. The participation, supported by the EU-funded Afghanistan Community Resilience Programme, aims to boost Afghanistan's export sector.

item.title: Russian missile strike on Ukrainian residential building kills at least 22
item.description: Rescuers searched for survivors in the rubble of a destroyed residential building in northern Ukraine following a Russian missile strike that killed at least 22 people. The attacks, occurring on October 7, are part of daily assaults by Russian forces amid growing difficulties on the front lines. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called them among the 'most vile' recent attacks.

item.title: Kazakhstan President highlights regional cooperation and challenges at Central Asia summit
item.description: Kazakhstan's President addressed the Central Asia and Azerbaijan leaders' meeting, emphasizing the region's growth and geopolitical importance. He highlighted the untapped potential of internal markets, proposing a joint action plan. The President also pointed to water scarcity as a major challenge and stressed the need for cooperation in artificial intelligence and combating digital threats.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA denies reports of 14 citizens sent from conflict zone to Russia
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied reports claiming 14 Kazakh citizens were sent from a conflict zone to the Kazakh embassy in Russia. The ministry stated that spreading unverified information about citizens in conflict zones is unacceptable and misleads families. They continue to engage with Russian authorities on the matter and will provide updates.

item.title: Almaty showcases progress on construction of its Light Rail Transit (LRT) depot
item.description: Almaty residents have been shown the construction progress of the depot for the city's Light Rail Transit (LRT) project. The depot is being built in the Alatau district's Industrial Zone. A subcontractor, QPARK GROUP, has shared a video update, indicating the project is 20% complete, involving significant soil excavation and replacement to ensure structural stability.

item.title: Tokayev highlights regional threats: terrorism, drug trafficking, arms, human trade
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has identified significant regional threats, including terrorism, drug trafficking, illicit arms trade, and human trafficking. He addressed these dangers in a statement concerning the security of Central Asian nations.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA Denies Reports of 14 Citizens Returning from Combat Zones
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied social media reports claiming 14 Kazakh citizens were returning from combat zones and would be brought to the republic's embassy in Russia. The ministry stated that spreading unverified information is unacceptable and misleads families awaiting news. They continue to engage with Russian authorities on the matter.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Wanted Internationally for Human Trafficking Arrested in Turkey
item.description: An Uzbek citizen, identified as M.X., who was internationally wanted for human trafficking and illegal departure from the country, has been apprehended in Turkey. The arrest was made through cooperation between Uzbek and Turkish law enforcement agencies. M.X. is accused of deceiving individuals and forcing them into prostitution in Thailand and Turkey.

item.title: UN OCHA: $160 Million Needed for Afghanistan's Education Needs by 2026
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) stated that $160 million is required to meet Afghanistan's educational needs by 2026, with only $22 million secured so far. OCHA highlighted shortages in teachers, classrooms, and resources, particularly impacting girls barred from secondary education. The agency urged lifting the ban on girls' education.

item.title: Businessman Illegally Uproots 586 Trees in Bostanliq, Causing 1.7 Billion Som Damage
item.description: In Bostanliq district, Tashkent region, a businessman illegally uprooted 586 trees, including valuable species. The National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change reported the incident, stating that despite prior warnings, the entrepreneur resisted. Environmental police have intervened, and the estimated damage to nature is 1.7 billion som.

item.title: President Proposes Youth Forum on Volunteering, Emphasizing Central Asian Cooperation
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed holding a youth forum on volunteering next year under the slogan 'Central Asia – A Hub of Good Deeds'. He suggested creating a unified calendar of cultural, scientific, and sports events for Central Asia and Azerbaijan to boost tourism and people-to-people exchanges. The president also stressed the importance of direct dialogue among leaders.

item.title: Central Asian Leaders Discuss Caspian Sea Cargo Flow and Water Management
item.description: Leaders of Central Asian nations met to discuss initiatives aimed at increasing Caspian Sea cargo traffic fourfold by 2040. They also addressed water resource management challenges, proposing new approaches based on mutual respect and equality, potentially through a new regional convention or a UN-backed international water organization. The development of cross-border logistics and industrial cooperation zones was also highlighted.

item.title: Uzbekistan Approves New Regulations for Victims of Human Trafficking
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved new regulations for social services provided to victims of human trafficking. Victims can receive free accommodation in specialized institutions for up to six months. Support includes emergency medical, psychological, and legal aid, document restoration, and job placement assistance.

item.title: Kazakh President Proposes Central Asian Partnership on Artificial Intelligence
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed establishing a Central Asian partnership focused on artificial intelligence during the 8th Consultative Meeting of Heads of State. This initiative aims to foster collaboration among scientific centers, universities, and tech companies in the region for information and experience exchange. Kazakhstan also suggested developing a joint declaration on the responsible use of AI.

item.title: Tokayev Demands Review of Over 200 Central Asian Initiatives
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that less than half of the over 200 initiatives proposed by Central Asian countries since 2018 have been implemented. Speaking at the 8th Consultative Meeting of Heads of State, he called for a review of regional initiatives by foreign ministries to assess their relevance and potential. He also proposed expanding Kazakhstan's 'Clean Kazakhstan' project to the regional level.

item.title: Central Asian Leaders and Azerbaijan Sign Joint Statement on Regional Cooperation
item.description: Leaders from Central Asia and Azerbaijan have signed a joint statement following the 8th Consultative Meeting of Heads of State. Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted the region's role as a center for growth and geopolitical interaction, emphasizing peace, unity, and mutual support in addressing contemporary challenges.

item.title: Tokayev Proposes Increasing Intra-Regional Trade to $20 Billion
item.description: At the 8th Consultative Meeting of Central Asian and Azerbaijani Heads of State, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed a joint action plan to increase intra-regional trade from the current $13 billion (8% of total trade) to at least $20 billion. He also emphasized the need for joint approaches to control critical technologies, including artificial intelligence.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan Deepen Strategic Partnership for Regional Stability
item.description: Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are entering a new phase of strategic partnership, crucial for regional stability amidst global uncertainty. Their cooperation in security, economy, energy, transport, water resources, and humanitarian ties is vital. This partnership, built on political trust and economic complementarity, enhances predictability for trade and investment across Central Asia.

item.title: Kazakh President emphasizes developing the Trans-Caspian International Transport Corridor
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted the potential of trade and logistics hubs near borders and industrial cooperation centers. He stated that developing the Trans-Caspian International Transport Corridor is a priority, noting increased demand for the Middle Corridor. Kazakhstan is also developing its transport infrastructure, including new railway lines.

item.title: Kazakh President attends 8th Consultative Meeting of Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev attended the 8th Consultative Meeting of Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan. He noted the symbolic significance of the meeting coinciding with the 35th anniversary of independence for these nations. Kazakhstan presented its position on key regional cooperation issues.

item.title: Afghanistan's Freedom Front Claims Killing Five Taliban Members in Badakhshan Attack
item.description: The Freedom Front of Afghanistan reported that five Taliban members were killed in an attack on their vehicle in Kiran wa Manjan district, Badakhshan province. The incident occurred on Tuesday evening as the vehicle traveled from Kiran wa Manjan towards Panjshir. The group also claimed the Taliban are inciting propaganda against opposition groups.

item.title: Blackouts to Become Norm, Tariffs to Rise: How to Prepare for the Energy Crisis?
item.description: The article discusses the potential for widespread blackouts and rising energy tariffs, suggesting these could become the new norm. It poses the question of how individuals and the region can prepare for an impending energy crisis, implying a need for proactive measures and adaptation strategies.

item.title: Tajikistan and KOICA Discuss Investment and Joint Projects in Economic Development
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Economic Development and Trade met with the Executive Director of KOICA's Global Leaders Program to discuss trade-economic cooperation, investment attraction, and joint projects. Discussions included digitalization, human capital development, intellectual property, and investment expansion. Trade turnover exceeded $150 million in 2024.

item.title: Herat Residents Face Severe Drinking Water Shortages Amid Deepening Crisis
item.description: Herat residents, like 50-year-old Rahila, are experiencing severe drinking water shortages, sometimes waiting days for access. The scarcity is attributed to factors including extensive groundwater pumping for agriculture, leading to wells being significantly deeper. Residents report a stark contrast to past abundance, highlighting the growing pressure on water supplies in the region.

item.title: Tajikistan President Urges Enhanced Economic and Energy Cooperation in Central Asia
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon of Tajikistan called for closer economic, transport, energy, and industrial collaboration among Central Asian nations and Azerbaijan. Speaking at a summit in Turkmenistan, he highlighted the region's resources for joint ventures and industrial development, emphasizing the need for digital and green technologies, innovation, and AI adoption. He also stressed improving supply chains and adapting products to international market requirements.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Hungary Expand Cooperation in Education and Innovation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Hungary are set to deepen their collaboration in higher education, science, innovation, and talent development. A meeting at the Uzbek Embassy in Hungary discussed joint initiatives between Óbuda University and Uzbek institutions, including the Jizzakh Science and Innovation Technopark. Both sides expressed interest in expanding partnerships in engineering, AI, digital technologies, and emergency management.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Revise Polyclinic Performance Evaluation System with New Criteria
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health is changing how polyclinics are evaluated. New criteria will include waiting times for specialists, timely diagnostic tests, and post-discharge patient follow-up. A unified 100-point system will automatically calculate indicators quarterly based on health information system data, aiming for objective quality assessment.

item.title: Pakistan's PM Urges UN Chief to Act Against Terror Groups Operating from Afghanistan
item.description: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres, calling for peace in Afghanistan and concrete action against terrorist groups using Afghan territory. Sharif emphasized dialogue and diplomacy for dispute resolution. Taliban officials deny harboring such groups and using Afghan soil against neighbors.

item.title: Five Sentenced to Prison for Beating Man to Death in Surxondaryo Over Property Dispute
item.description: In Denov district, Surxondaryo region, five individuals were sentenced to 4 to 9 years in prison for beating a 32-year-old man to death during a property dispute. The victim was assaulted and forcibly taken to another district, where the violence continued before he was abandoned at a medical facility, later succumbing to his injuries.

item.title: Central Asian and Azerbaijani Leaders Convene in Avaza for Consultative Meeting
item.description: Leaders from Central Asian nations and Azerbaijan will gather in Turkmenistan's Avaza tourist zone on October 8 for the eighth consultative meeting. The Caspian Ecological Summit and the CIS summit will follow on October 9, with expected participation from Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.

item.title: Son of Kyrgyzstan's Former President Atambaev Sentenced to Four Years in Prison
item.description: The Pervomaysky District Court of Bishkek sentenced Kadyrbek Atambaev, son of former Kyrgyzstan President Almazbek Atambaev, to four years for violent seizure of power. Party leader Temirlan Sultanbekov received seven years. The court acquitted politician Kubanbek Kadyrov.

item.title: Protests in Europe, Airport and Tanker Attacks, Divorces and Scandals Reported Globally
item.description: Student protests continue in France and Belgium, with hundreds of institutions suspending classes. In Spain, a tenant rights movement gained momentum after an elderly woman's eviction. The Middle East saw attacks on Saudi airports and a tanker off Qatar. South Korea is investigating alleged oil product shipments to Russia.

item.title: CSTO Contingents from Four Nations Deploy to Belarus for Joint Exercises
item.description: Peacekeeping, CBRN defense, and medical support units from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Russia, and Tajikistan are moving to Belarus for the 'Indestructible Brotherhood-2026' and 'Barrier-2026' exercises. The drills, held October 12-16, aim to enhance coordination and readiness for collective security tasks.
